title: LZ4 frame format
summary: LZ4 is an extremely fast compression algorithm. The LZ4 frame format: 4-byte magic (0x184D2204), frame descriptor (flags + optional content size + dictionary ID + content checksum flag), then blocks (each with a 4-byte size, compressed or uncompressed), then an end mark (0x00000000) and optional content checksum.

ext.summary: LZ4 is an extremely fast compression algorithm. The LZ4 frame format: 4-byte magic (0x184D2204), frame descriptor (flags + optional content size + dictionary ID + content checksum flag), then blocks (each with a 4-byte size, compressed or uncompressed), then an end mark (0x00000000) and optional content checksum.

structure.meaning: Bit 7-6: version (01), bit 5: block independence, bit 4: block checksum, bit 3: content size, bit 2: content checksum, bit 1-0: reserved (0).
Size of uncompressed content (if FLG content size flag set).
ID of the dictionary (if FLG reserved/dict flag set).
Header checksum (XXH32 of the header bytes, low byte).
4-byte block size (MSB = uncompressed flag) + block data. Size 0 = end mark.
XXH32 of the uncompressed content (if FLG content checksum flag set).

ext.example_decoded: LZ4 magic + frame descriptor (version 1, 64KB blocks, no content size/checksum)
notes: LZ4 achieves ~500 MB/s+ compression and ~2 GB/s+ decompression.
Block independence: each block can be decompressed independently (random access).
LZ4 is used by ZFS, Linux kernel (module compression), Hadoop, and many databases.
The raw LZ4 block format (without frame) is simpler: token (4 bits literal length + 4 bits match length) + literals + offset + extra lengths.
